description:
COMPOSITION LAYER: instructions become a composable library; the orchestrator (POLYBIUS/PLINY) selects which modules a task needs and points the sub-agent at them AT DISPATCH TIME. Compaction-proof because the selection rides the dispatch payload, delivered fresh at spawn.

Three delivery channels - all use tools every agent already has (no Skill-grant; see the CLI-not-MCP decision):
- inline in dispatch prompt: small, task-specific instruction.
- disk module (.claude/modules/X.md) via Read: stable, reused across tasks/projects; orchestrator names the path in the dispatch.
- bw ticket via bw show <id>: dynamic / bespoke / single-use, OR anything that must persist or be shared.

bw one-offs are NOT a curated skill library - they are the routine custom-instruction stream the orchestrator generates constantly, retained in bw for RECORD-KEEPING (audit trail of what each agent was told). Recurrence in that record is the SIGNAL to author a reusable disk module. So the bw log FEEDS the module library; it is not itself the library. (PRINCIPAL clarification 2026-05-22.)

ORCHESTRATOR ROUTING MAP: a small structured table (task type -> modules to load) lives in the orchestrator's slim core (always-needed, no trigger). Should itself be checkable (a hook can verify the expected modules were referenced for a given task type).

PRECEDENT: PLINY dispatch briefs already inject task context (MAJOR_PLINY 5.2 ADA preamble, 5.2.1 credential cite, "run bw start <id>..."). This formalizes an existing primitive into a first-class module system - evolutionary, not new.

WEAK SPOT: a sub-agent that compacts mid-task has no orchestrator re-telling it (no cron/hook of its own). It can re-read its bw ticket only if prompted. Mitigation: keep sub-agent tasks bounded (ties to the enforcement-layer re-decompose remediation).

title: Composition layer: instruction-module library + orchestrator routing (bw/disk/dispatch)
